title: Rigidity of already given coherent relative dualizing pairs
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a separated flat locally finitely presented morphism of schemes with $S$ locally Noetherian [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-flat-morphism], [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Put $Y=X\times_SX$ with first projection $p_1$ and closed diagonal $\Delta$. A relative dualizing pair in this statement means a given object $K\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ which is pseudo-coherent and locally has finite Tor amplitude over $S$, together with a map $\xi:\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\to Lp_1^*K$ such that multiplication by $\xi$ gives an isomorphism $\Delta_*\mathcal O_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\mathcal Hom_Y(\Delta_*\mathcal O_X,Lp_1^*K)$ [def-pc-derived-category], [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex], [def-pc-derived-pullback], [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. For any such pair the scalar map $\mathcal O_X\to R\mathcal Hom_X(K,K)$ is an isomorphism. Given two such pairs $(K,\xi)$ and $(L,\eta)$, there is exactly one isomorphism $\alpha:K\to L$ with $(Lp_1^*\alpha)\xi=\eta$. The same assertions apply to any open restriction $U\to S$ of $f$. This statement assumes the pairs are already supplied and asserts no existence of a pair.

source.place: Tags 0E2T (given pair definition), 0E2V (scalar derived endomorphisms), 0E2W (unique class-preserving isomorphism).

proof.text: For the scalar assertion use the supplied pair twice, setting $(L,\eta)=(K,\xi)$; for uniqueness use the two given pairs. Choose the basis of affine $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ mapping into Noetherian affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset S$. These opens form a basis: inside any neighbourhood of $x$, choose such a $V$ about $f(x)$ and an affine neighbourhood of $x$ in its inverse image. Apply affine diagonal comparison to each supplied pair: $R\to A$ is flat finitely presented with $A$ Noetherian, and $K|_U,L|_U$ correspond to pseudo-coherent $A$-complexes $M,N$ of finite $R$-Tor amplitude, with their actual diagonal classes inducing the required multiplication isomorphisms. The localization/realization lemma identifies their scalar maps and class-preserving morphisms with the geometric ones. Since $V\hookrightarrow S$ is a monomorphism, $U\times_VU=U\times_SU$, so the affine and geometric diagonal classes have the same ambient open.

Apply algebraic diagonal normalization to $R\to A,M,N$ and the two classes. Its polynomial comparison object supplies scalar derived endomorphisms for $M$; its normalization supplies exactly one class-preserving isomorphism $M\to N$ and negative self-Ext vanishing. The realization lemma gives on each basis open the scalar-map isomorphism, a unique normalized $\alpha_U:K|_U\to L|_U$, and $\operatorname{Hom}(K|_U,K|_U[i])=0$ for $i<0$.

source.place: Tag 0E2V, lemma-relative-dualizing-RHom, and 0E2W, affine normalization; dualizing.tex 0BZW, 0E2E and 0E2D.

proof.text: The scalar-map comparison in the realization lemma identifies these local scalar maps with restrictions of the global one. Each cohomology sheaf of its cone restricts to zero on the covering basis, so every section is zero by the sheaf axiom. Thus the cone is zero and the global scalar map is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0E2V, locality of the scalar-map isomorphism.

proof.text: For a basis inclusion $W\subset U$, restriction compatibility from Step 1 makes $\alpha_U|_W$ class-preserving; local uniqueness from Step 2 gives $\alpha_U|_W=\alpha_W$. Apply diagonal-class basis descent to $K,L,\xi,\eta$. Its negative self-Ext and unique local normalization hypotheses are Step 2; its multiplication hypothesis is the supplied condition on $(L,\eta)$. It yields the unique global class-preserving isomorphism. Its identification of the class module with $\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$ detects equality of diagonal classes on the basis.

source.place: Tag 0E2W, lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing, last paragraph and normalization.

proof.text: For any open $W\subset X$, the localization lemma retains the geometric hypotheses and restricts supplied pairs and their multiplication maps to $W/S$. Apply Steps 1--4 to this morphism, also to any pairs supplied directly on $W$. This proves both open assertions. For empty $W$ the category of module sheaves and its derived category are zero, giving the same conclusions.
